s: The abstract concerns CLERC, a dataset created with legal professionals to support systems that assist with legal writing. s: This unit reports experiments with CLERC on legal citation retrieval and legal analysis generation. In generation, providing the texts of cited cases improves citation coverage, precision, and hallucination-related scores, although generated analyses still have serious factual and analytical limitations.

l: CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The abstract concerns large language models (LLMs) and their use in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for natural language processing. It identifies limitations in traditional RAG systems, including disrupted contextual integrity from text chunking and over-reliance on semantic similarity for retrieval. It introduces CausalRAG, which incorporates causal graphs into the retrieval process by constructing and tracing causal relationships. The framework is reported to outperform regular RAG and graph-based RAG across several metrics, improving retrieval precision, contextual continuity, and response accuracy and interpretability.

s: The unit describes how large language models (LLMs) have advanced natural language processing and enabled many applications. It explains that reliance on pre-trained knowledge limits LLMs’ ability to integrate and reason over dynamically updated external information, especially in academic research. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is presented as a framework that combines retrieval mechanisms with generative capabilities to improve contextual understanding and response quality. Recent research is described as focusing on two primary directions for improving RAG, although the unit provides only the beginning of the first direction.

l: CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening
s: The unit concerns limitations in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), especially disrupted context, reliance on semantic similarity over causal relevance, and inaccurate document selection. It introduces CausalRAG, which uses causal graphs to identify causal relationships in external knowledge and retrieve context that is both relevant and causally grounded. The authors evaluate CausalRAG against regular RAG and graph-based RAG across diverse domains and context lengths using answer faithfulness, context recall, and context precision. The reported results show that CausalRAG improves retrieval and generation quality, mitigates hallucinations, and produces more contextually rich and causally detailed responses.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, opening

These limitations can lead to seemingly relevant but shallow responses that lack essential details.

Its evaluation reports improvements in answer faithfulness, context recall, and context precision, along with reduced hallucinations and greater interpretability.

l: CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs
s: This unit reviews retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), graph-based RAG, and the emerging use of causal graphs in RAG. It argues that regular RAG can disrupt linguistic coherence through chunking, retrieve superficially similar but causally irrelevant information through semantic search, and amplify bias during generation. It reports that GraphRAG and related graph-based methods generally improve context precision through graph ranking and summarization but may reduce context recall by omitting relevant information. The unit introduces CausalRAG as a framework intended to address these limitations through causally grounded retrieval.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs
s: Retrieval-augmented generation enhances large language models' ability to handle knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating external knowledge retrieval. Research on it focuses on improving retrieval and integration mechanisms, as well as representing and using external knowledge for deeper reasoning and generation.

l: regular RAG, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs
s: Regular RAG commonly chunks documents into minimal units, which can disrupt natural linguistic and logical connections. Its semantic search can retrieve information that is superficially similar but causally irrelevant, and low retrieval precision can introduce bias that reduces generation accuracy.

l: graph-based RAG, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs
s: Graph-based RAG improves retrieved-context quality by summarizing and ranking graph information before retrieval. However, subgraph summarization may fail to remove all irrelevant information and may reduce recall by omitting less graph-central but causally relevant context.

l: causal graphs in RAG, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs
s: The direct integration of causal graphs into RAG architectures is described as largely unexplored. s: Subgraph summarization is used in graph-based RAG retrieval to condense graph information and improve context precision. The unit states that it may leave some irrelevant information and omit less graph-central but causally relevant context, thereby reducing recall.

l: CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Methodology .. Retrieving Context Causally
s: This unit introduces CausalRAG, a framework that integrates retrieval-augmented generation with causality to improve context retrieval from uploaded documents. It constructs a text-based graph whose nodes and edges represent entities, concepts, and relationships, then matches a user query to initial nodes and expands along graph edges to identify causal paths. A large language model estimates these paths, builds a refined causal graph, and generates a causal summary as grounded context. The summary is combined with the user query in a refined prompt for the final retrieval-augmented generation response.

l: CausalRAG, CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Methodology .. Retrieving Context Causally
s: CausalRAG integrates retrieval-augmented generation with causality by constructing text-based graphs from uploaded documents and retrieving information along causally linked paths. It uses a causal summary as retrieval context to improve contextual coherence, precision, and grounding.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Abstract
s: The abstract concerns PIC, a document chunking method for retrieval-augmented generation that uses document summaries as pseudo-instructions. It addresses limitations of rule-based chunking methods, which can produce overly large or semantically incomplete chunks, and semantic-based approaches, which may require costly large language model calls or fail to group related sentences adaptively. PIC computes semantic similarity between sentences and a document summary to dynamically form chunks aligned with key themes and potential user instructions. Experiments on multiple open-domain question-answering benchmarks show improved retrieval accuracy and end-to-end QA performance without additional training.
